newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens on renewed foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens on renewed foreign demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling suffered fresh losses on Monday on renewed demand for the dollar from foreign investors pulling out of a nervous market under seige from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), commercial bank dealers said.
The battered shilling was trading at a commercial mean of 69.76 against the dollar in early afternoon from the morning opening of 68.87 -- a 1.29 percent decline.
"The market is clearly one-sided. There is some good demand from offshore investors," a senior dealer from a leading commercial bank told Reuters.
"It's a combination. Most still want to get out while others are taking positions because they think the shilling will weaken more," he added.

The shilling sunk to a new official record low against the dollar of 70.26 on Thursday at the end of a slide since the IMF halted a $205 million aid package on July 31 in a row over corruption and governance.

Market analysts said the major reason for the shilling's slide was a loss in confidence by foreign investors, who no longer sure of the country's economic stability, were getting out at whatever price.
"It's not so much the fact that we lost the money but that we were blacklisted by the IMF, and investors use the IMF credit rating to determine where they will take their money," one analyst said.
Dealers said they were getting orders of upto $20 million and that at high prices -- 70.50 -- 71.50.
"Today there are no local (demand) orders. It's all from offshore investors and I don't think the local market (interbank) can support it," a senior dealer from a foreign bank told Reuters.
On Friday, the shilling picked up marginally as exporters sold dollars following the shilling record fall.
